writeup: TIC 251663993 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 7.310545 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 0.05%, with a detection significance of 15.7 in the BLS periodogram. Pixel-level imaging analysis confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 7.1, though the centroid offset of 13.0 arcsec warrants attention. Notably, the eclipse depths alternate significantly between cycles, which suggests the initially measured period was actually half the true orbital period. No secondary eclipse was detected, and the candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The machine-learning screening score of 0.82 indicates moderate confidence that this represents a genuine astrophysical source rather than an artifact.
